cards.text: Jehoshaphat, king of Judah, rests with his fathers and is buried in the City of David. His son Jehoram reigns in his place. Jehoram has six brothers, and their dad gave them silver, gold and fortified cities in Judah, but the kingdom goes to Jehoram.

cards.question: Six brothers get silver, gold and cities. Why does the kingdom go to Jehoram?

answers.text: He won a battle for it

cards.question: Once Jehoram has established himself over his father's kingdom, he strengthens himself by putting all his ___ to the sword.
Jehoram's brothers are the only ones he puts to the sword.

cards.text: Jehoram is thirty-two when he becomes king, and he reigns in Jerusalem eight years. He walks in the ways of the kings of Israel, just as the house of Ahab, a king of Israel, had done.

cards.question: Jehoram walks just like the house of Ahab. The text says why: he married a daughter of ___.

cards.text: Jehoram does evil in the sight of the LORD. Yet the LORD won't destroy the house of David, since He had promised to maintain a lamp for David and his descendants forever.

cards.question: Jehoram is doing evil, but the LORD won't destroy the house of David. Along with His promise of a lamp, what's the other reason?

cards.text: Then, in Jehoram's days, Edom rebels against the hand of Judah. Edom basically puts in its two weeks' notice, friend. Except there are no two weeks!

cards.question: Edom rebels against the hand of Judah and appoints their own ___.
Jehoram goes after Edom with just a handful of men.

cards.text: Jehoram crosses into Edom with his officers and all his chariots. And then the Edomites surround him and his chariot commanders, like a surprise party where NOBODY is happy to see you.

cards.question: Surrounded by the Edomites, what does Jehoram do?

answers.text: He rises up and attacks by night
He surrenders to Edom's new king
He sends gold to buy peace

cards.text: Even so, Edom stays in rebellion against Judah to this day, and at the same time, the town of Libnah rebels too. Two at once. That's my oven timer and my smoke alarm going off TOGETHER.

cards.question: Libnah rebels against Jehoram too. What reason does the text give?

cards.text: Jehoram also builds high places on the hills of Judah. He causes the people of Jerusalem to prostitute themselves and leads Judah astray.
Then Jehoram hears from Elijah, a prophet of the LORD. Not face to face, though.

cards.question: Elijah the prophet has a message from the LORD for Jehoram. How does it reach him?
Elijah's letter says Jehoram has NOT walked in the ways of which kings?
Elijah's letter says the brothers Jehoram killed were better than him.

cards.text: The letter keeps going: the LORD is about to strike Jehoram's people, his sons, his wives and all his possessions with a serious blow. I spent years next to old takeout menus in that drawer, and not ONE of them ever delivered news like this.

cards.question: Day after day, the letter says, Jehoram himself will suffer from a severe ___.

cards.text: Then the LORD stirs up the spirit of some neighbors against Jehoram.

cards.question: Who does the LORD stir up against Jehoram?

cards.text: They invade Judah and carry off everything in the king's palace, plus his sons and his wives. That's the serious blow Elijah's letter warned about.

cards.question: Out of all Jehoram's sons, who is the only one left to him?

cards.text: After all this, the LORD afflicts Jehoram with an incurable disease of the bowels, just as Elijah's letter said.

cards.question: Jehoram's disease goes on day after day for two full ___.

cards.text: In the end, Jehoram dies in severe pain.

cards.question: When Jehoram dies, his people make a fire in his honor, like they did for his fathers.

cards.text: The text says Jehoram died to no one's regret. He's buried in the City of David.

cards.question: Jehoram is buried in the City of David, but not in the tombs of the ___.

findings.problem: Card 5 already ties Jehoram to the house of Ahab, and the question itself opens with 'Jehoram walks just like the house of Ahab.' That points straight at 'Ahab' and rules out Jeroboam and Baasha before the baker picks.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: 'Even so, Edom stays in rebellion' adds a contrast, as if the rebellion went on in spite of Jehoram's night attack. The BSB says only 'So to this day Edom has been in rebellion' and leaves the link to the attack open.

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.

findings.problem: Asa first appears in this passage as part of the right answer, with nothing to say who he is. The text calls him 'Asa king of Judah' (2 Chr 21:12).

rule.text: New people. The first time someone shows up, he says simply who they are, like "Cyrus, king of Persia" or "Moses, Israel's leader."

findings.problem: 'By a royal herald' overlaps with the right answer. A letter has to be carried by someone, so a baker could argue a herald brought it. The wrong answer should be a clearly different way of getting a message.

rule.text: No near-matches. A wrong answer never means the same as the right answer, or close to it. If a baker could argue it's right, replace it.

findings.problem: The takeout menu joke doesn't match the core action. A prophet's letter announcing judgment and a menu that never 'delivered news' are not the same action, so the line needs a beat to work out.

rule.text: The everyday comparison must have the same action.

findings.problem: 'That's the serious blow Elijah's letter warned about' states a link the text doesn't state. Verses 16-17 never say the invasion was the fulfillment of verse 14. The letter also named 'your people,' which the invasion card doesn't cover.

rule.text: Connecting passages. When he connects two passages, or explains what a law was for, he says only what the texts state.

findings.problem: Both wrong answers say the same thing ('his eldest' and 'his firstborn'), so 'his youngest' stands out as the odd one. Both also reuse Azariah and Michael, who are Jehoram's brothers in verse 2. That mixes up the passage's own people instead of drawing on other real details.

rule.text: All the answers are the same kind of thing, about the same length and the same tone. None are silly.

findings.problem: Most story cards outside stop 1 cards 9, 12 and 14 and stop 2 card 6 have no Papa Dorin voice at all. Examples are stop 1 card 1, stop 2 card 1, card 8, card 12 and card 14 ('In the end, Jehoram dies in severe pain.'). Stop 2 has only one attempt at humor in 17 cards.

rule.text: Short, but not stripped down. A story card still has enough of Papa Dorin's voice and enough context that the moment makes sense.
